verification_report.summary: The proof is correct. The finite-flat radial cutoff proves that the curvature measure of a continuous CLD-psh function has no atom at a rigid point. The source-separated tropical localization, Euclidean edge-density calculation, full-star balancing, type-3 comparison, and type-2 residual-divisor/Riemann--Roch argument give one global nonnegative coefficient on a connected rig-smooth curve. Finite normalization, the locally finite rigid conductor/intersection locus, and vanishing of smooth top-degree test germs there then give the unique component-current classification on a reduced pure curve; the rigid zero-atom lemma prevents cancellation of component curvature measures and proves the continuous-psh Bedford--Taylor conclusion. For the rigid-exception extension, normality makes every exceptional rigid point unibranch, whereas every interior point of an injective arc is pluribranch, so the rig-smooth complement is nonempty and connected. Smooth rigidity holds on that complement, and the d_K support theorem makes every smooth (1,1)-test form avoid the exceptional set, extending the scalar current identity to X. Finally, multiplication of the integration current by u-v agrees with the function current [u-v], so equal curvatures give the asserted continuous-psh independence. All cited CLD, Ducros, GJR, and Tate statements match their definitions, hypotheses, and uses.
